---
title: CDN cache lifetime configuration
sidebarTitle: Configure CDN caching
ai-navigation: Configure CDN cache lifetime with origin or CDN controlled settings, advanced caching rules, video time-to-live (TTL) guidance, and cache header verification.
---

Files cannot be stored in CDN servers' cache indefinitely. The CDN caching feature controls how long files from an origin server are stored in the CDN server's cache. When users request these files, they are served from cache without additional requests to the origin, reducing delivery time, costs, and origin server load.

<Note>
Files users have not requested within 36 hours will be removed from the CDN servers' cache, regardless of the feature settings.
</Note>

When a cached file's lifetime expires, Gcore CDN performs conditional revalidation with the origin if the cached response includes a validator such as an [ETag](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/ETag) or `Last-Modified` header. The CDN sends a conditional request (`If-None-Match` or `If-Modified-Since`); if the origin responds with 304 Not Modified, the cached copy is reused and its lifetime is reset. If the origin returns a new response, the CDN stores and serves the updated content.

If the cached response includes no validator, the CDN cannot perform conditional revalidation and must retrieve the full response from the origin after expiration.

## CDN caching configuration

The CDN caching feature has two options: Origin controlled (enabled by default) and CDN controlled. Select one to set the caching time either in the origin server's HTTP `Cache-Control` header or in the CDN settings.

<Info>
CDN caching eligibility is based on HTTP response status codes and `Cache-Control` headers, not on file extensions. All file types—including `.webp`, `.swf`, and others—follow the same caching rules as any other object.
</Info>

### Origin controlled

Set the `Cache-Control` header on the origin server, then configure the fallback cache expiry in the portal.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Configure Cache-Control on the origin server">
    Depending on the web server (Apache or Nginx), add the `Cache-Control` header with the `max-age` and `public` parameters to the `.htaccess` (for Apache) or `nginx.conf` (for Nginx) file.

    In `Cache-Control`, `public` permits shared-cache (CDN) storage, and `max-age` sets the freshness duration in seconds.

    The following Apache configuration caches `.gif` and `.ico` files for 4 days (`max-age=345600` seconds):

    ```
    <ifModule mod_headers.c>   
      <FilesMatch "\.(gif|ico)$">   
        Header set Cache-Control "max-age=345600, public"   
      </FilesMatch>   
    </ifModule>
    ```

    The following Nginx configuration caches `.ico`, `.css`, `.js`, `.gif`, `.jpeg`, and `.png` files for 1 day (86,400 seconds):

    ```
    server {   
     #...   
      location ~* \.(?:ico|css|js|gif|jpeg|png)$ {   
        add_header Cache-Control "max-age=86400, public";   
      }   
     #...   
    }
    ```
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open the CDN resource settings">
    In the [Gcore&nbsp;Customer&nbsp;Portal](https://portal.gcore.com), navigate to **CDN** > **CDN resources** and click the CNAME of the resource where the `Cache-Control` header is configured.

    <Frame>![CDN resources list page](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/specify-cache-lifetime-on-a-cdn-resource-or-origin/cdn-resources.png)</Frame>
  </Step>
  <Step title="Navigate to CDN caching">
    Navigate to **Cache** > **CDN caching**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Confirm Origin controlled is selected">
    Confirm that **Origin controlled** is selected in the dropdown.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Set the default cache expiry">
    Specify the timespan in the **Default cache expiry** field. Select a predefined value from the list or select **Custom value** and enter the time in seconds. This value is used as a fallback when the origin does not send caching HTTP headers.

    <Info>
    For Origin controlled mode, CDN servers cache responses with codes 200, 201, 204, 206, 301, 302, 303, 304, 307, and 308. Responses with other codes are not cached.
    </Info>

    <Frame>![CDN caching settings with Origin controlled selected](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/specify-cache-lifetime-on-a-cdn-resource-or-origin/cdn-caching-origin-controlled.png)</Frame>
  </Step>
  <Step title="Save changes">
    Click **Save changes**.
  </Step>
</Steps>

### CDN controlled

CDN caching can be configured at two levels:

  * For the whole resource

  * At the advanced caching rule level in the resource

These settings are independent — CDN caching can be set to **Do not cache** in the main settings while enabled in an advanced rule, and vice versa.

<Warning>
CDN caching applies only to responses with status codes 200, 206, 301, and 302. Responses with 4xx and 5xx status codes are not cached by default. To cache 404 or other non-default status codes, configure an advanced caching rule under the **Enable CDN caching via advanced caching rules** tab below.
</Warning>

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Enable CDN caching for the whole resource">
    <Steps>
      <Step title="Open CDN resources">
        In the Customer Portal, navigate to **CDN** > **CDN resources**.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Open the resource settings">
        Click the CNAME of the required resource to open its settings.

        <Frame>![CDN resources list page](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/specify-cache-lifetime-on-a-cdn-resource-or-origin/cdn-resources.png)</Frame>
      </Step>
      <Step title="Navigate to CDN caching">
        Navigate to **Cache** > **CDN caching**.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Enable CDN caching">
        Confirm the **Enable CDN caching** toggle is enabled. If not, click the toggle to enable it.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Select CDN controlled">
        Select **CDN controlled** from the dropdown.

        <Frame>![CDN caching settings with CDN controlled selected](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/specify-cache-lifetime-on-a-cdn-resource-or-origin/cdn-caching-cdn-controlled.png)</Frame>
      </Step>
      <Step title="Set the cache expiry">
        Specify the caching timespan in the **Cache expiry** field. Select a predefined value from the list or select **Custom value** and enter a time in seconds.

        This caching time applies to response codes 200, 206, 301, and 302. Responses with 4xx and 5xx are not cached.

        <Warning>
        If the **Do not cache** option is selected, caching is disabled even when the **Enable CDN caching** toggle is enabled.
        </Warning>
      </Step>
      <Step title="Configure advanced rules (optional)">
        Optionally, configure advanced caching rules for different caching times by response code.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Save changes">
        Click **Save changes**.
      </Step>
    </Steps>
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Enable CDN caching via advanced caching rules">
    <Steps>
      <Step title="Navigate to CDN caching">
        In the CDN resource settings, navigate to the **Cache** section.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Enable CDN caching">
        Confirm the **Enable CDN caching** toggle is enabled. If not, click the toggle to enable it.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Select CDN controlled">
        Select **CDN controlled** from the dropdown.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Add a caching rule">
        Click **Add rule** and configure it as follows:

          * **Response code**: enter the HTTP response code to apply caching to.

          * **Caching time**: specify how long the data will be stored in the cache before it expires.

        <Frame>![Advanced caching rule form with Response code and Caching time fields](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/specify-cache-lifetime-on-a-cdn-resource-or-origin/advanced-caching-rule.png)</Frame>

        The Caching time in advanced rules takes priority over the general Cache expiry.

        With a Cache expiry of four days and two advanced rules — one for the 200 response code configured for 10 minutes and another for 404 configured for one minute — requests are cached as follows:

          * Requests with response code 200: cached for 10 minutes.
          * Requests with response code 404: cached for one minute.
          * Requests with response codes 206, 301, and 302: cached for four days.
          * Requests with response codes 4xx (except 404) and 5xx: not cached.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Save changes">
        Click **Save changes** to apply the settings.
      </Step>
    </Steps>
  </Tab>
</Tabs>


## CDN caching verification

To verify that CDN caching is working correctly, inspect HTTP response headers using curl or browser DevTools.

### Verification with curl

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open a terminal">
    Open a terminal (macOS or Linux) or command prompt (Windows).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Run the command">
    Run the following command, replacing the URL with a file delivered via your CDN resource:

    ```sh
    curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://cdn.example.com/css/style.css
    ```

    The command sends a GET request and prints only the response headers. The example output below shows the key headers for cache diagnostics. For a description of each header, see [Caching response headers](#caching-response-headers).

    ```
    HTTP/2 200
    cache-control: max-age=86400, public
    cache: HIT
    x-cached-since: 2026-09-22T08:00:00+00:00
    x-id: ab-cd-e123
    ```

    For content caching issues, verify the origin settings or contact [Gcore&nbsp;Support](https://support.gcore.com/hc/en-us/requests/new).
  </Step>
</Steps>

### Browser DevTools verification

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open a web browser">
    Open a web browser.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Navigate to the website">
    Navigate to the website served via CDN.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open DevTools">
    Right-click and select **Inspect** to open DevTools.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Select the Network tab">
    Select the **Network** tab.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Refresh the page">
    Refresh the page.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Select a CDN-delivered file">
    Select any file from the list that is delivered via CDN.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Review response headers">
    On the **Headers** tab, review the response headers. The key cache-related headers are described in the [Caching response headers](#caching-response-headers) section.

    <Frame>![Browser DevTools Network tab showing response headers](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/specify-cache-lifetime-on-a-cdn-resource-or-origin/devtools-headers.png)</Frame>
  </Step>
</Steps>

### Caching response headers

There are several HTTP response headers that help analyze the state of the cache:

HTTP header | Explanation
---|---
CACHE: HIT | The file was served from the CDN cache. Caching is working correctly.
CACHE: MISS | The file was not in the CDN cache and was fetched from the origin. This occurs on the first request for a file that has not been cached yet, after the cached copy has expired and the origin returned a new response, or after a purge by URL. The response is stored in cache; subsequent requests for a cacheable file return CACHE: HIT.
CACHE: BYPASS | The CDN cache was skipped and the file was served directly from the origin without being stored. This occurs after a full purge (purge all) or purge by pattern, or when the response carries a `Cache-Control: no-store` or `Cache-Control: no-cache` directive. By standard (`no-store` prohibits caching; `no-cache` permits storage but requires revalidation), Gcore CDN treats both directives as uncacheable. Unlike CACHE: MISS, the response is not stored in cache.
X-ID: ab-cd-d123 | Identifier of the Gcore CDN edge server that delivered the file. Resolve `{x-id}.fe.gc.onl` using `nslookup` or `dig` to get the server's IP address — useful for [cache&nbsp;diagnostics](/cdn/troubleshooting/cache-percentage-is-low-how-to-solve-the-issue).
X-Cached-Since: 2023-02-23T14:33:07+00:00 | The time when the file was cached in the CDN server in UTC.



## Video cache recommendations

Video files, video on demand (VOD) or live video, need different cache lifetimes by file type. Cache segments and single-file MP4 content longer, while keeping manifests short so players receive fresh live and playlist updates.

For video-specific values, apply the [caching&nbsp;rules](/cdn/getting-started/create-a-cdn-resource/create-a-cdn-resource-for-video-streaming#step-4-configure-caching-rules) used when creating a CDN resource for video streaming. They include recommended time-to-live (TTL) values for MP4, HLS, MPEG-DASH, live manifests, and segment files.
